From the example above, we see that in order to investigate the mul- tiplicative principle carefully, we need to consider ordered pairs. We should define this carefully: Cartesian Product. Given sets A and B , we can form the set A × B | {( x , y ) : x ∈ A ∧ y ∈ B } to be the set of all ordered pairs ( x , y ) where x is an element of A and y is an element of B . We call A × B the Cartesian product of A and B .
